name: Reflex

modes.label: Hosted Python apps
modes.note: Compute = machine type (CPU/RAM allocated per instance, e.g. 'c2m4') x number of regions x instance runtime; idle instances accrue nothing and wake on request; Persistent Machine 'Coming soon'. Per-machine-type prices are not published anywhere public (only via 'reflex cloud vmtypes' when logged in). Default region sjc.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 1 published app on Reflex Cloud, shared compute, limited AI generation + hosting usage that 'refills periodically' (amount not published), public apps/repos only, 1 workspace user, 7-day logs, no always-on (apps idle-sleep), no custom domains.

plans.name: Pro 25
plans.note: Pro variants $25/$50/$100/$200 give the same dollar amount as a monthly allowance shared by AI generation (AI Builder credits) and app hosting. No published overage: 'Choose a higher Pro monthly usage allowance for more capacity.' 1 workspace user; multiple apps; shared or dedicated compute; multi-region; always-on deployments; 90-day logs. Same note applies to Pro 50/100/200.

caveats: Free 1 published app with periodically refilled limited usage. Pro $25/$50/$100/$200 monthly allowance shared by AI generation and hosting. No session limits does not mean unlimited CPU-hours.

Shared/dedicated deployment sizes and regions offered but no per-vCPU/RAM list tariff on pricing page. Enterprise on own Google Cloud, SSO, on-prem and air-gap options quote. Open-source Apache-2.0 framework is not free managed infrastructure.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Seats: 'Each organization member uses a seat. A pending invitation also holds a seat'. Seat price is not published; Free and Pro allow 1 workspace user, more users/team workspaces are Enterprise (contact sales).

BYOC (Enterprise only) deploys to your own AWS ECS, Google Cloud Run or Azure Container Apps via 'reflex cloud deploy --aws/--gcp/--azure'; managed Google Cloud connection also Enterprise. Self-host on-prem/air-gapped is Enterprise.

fleet.tiers: Free includes 1 hosted app on shared compute; Pro provides higher hosting usage; enterprise app limits customized.
fleet.notes: One hosted app is not necessarily one VM: deployment can use multiple regions and managed instance lifecycle. No aggregate new-account instance/vCPU/GPU quota established; persistent machines not yet available per compute docs.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The deployment form may show a disabled Persistent Machine option. This feature is not available yet. When disabled, Reflex manages app instances and can scale them down when idle.
snapshot_auto.note: Managed stateless app instances; idle instances scale down and wake on request with no state saved ('include_db' local SQLite 'is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts'). AI Builder auto-creates source-code checkpoints per agent message (restore-checkpoint) - app source only, not machine state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A rollback redeploys a previous deployment's stored image and makes it current without rebuilding from source
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine/disk snapshot API. Only deployment-image history/rollback, Builder source checkpoints, and Fork/Copy app (copies source files).

secret_proxy.quote: Apps receive the values as environment variables at runtime.
secret_proxy.note: Project/app secrets and integration credentials become env vars read via os.environ; 'Sensitive' mode hides values from team members only. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: This database is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts. Use a database service for production data.
volume_attach.note: No volumes in cloud.yml or docs; 'Persistent Machine' is marked 'Coming soon' on machine-types page. Use external DB/storage integrations.

volume_shared.note: No first-party volumes or shared filesystems documented.
